It takes a lot of courage to reach out for help, especially when past experiences with therapy have been disappointing. It is completely understandable to feel hesitant about trying it again when it didn't work for your PTSD four years ago. Healing is not a one-size-fits-all process, and it is okay that your previous experience wasn't the right fit.

Since traditional talk therapy didn't feel helpful, you might want to explore specialized trauma approaches like EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) or somatic experiencing, which focus more on how the body processes trauma rather than just talking. Support groups can also connect you with others who truly understand what you are going through. Reaching out to a primary care doctor could be another good starting point to discuss alternative treatments, medications, or local resources. Please don't give up on finding the support that works best for you.
